Alice is bored on the riverbank while her sister reads.
A White Rabbit runs by, talking to himself and checking a watch.
Alice follows the Rabbit down a big rabbit hole.
Alice falls slowly down a deep hole and thinks of her cat Dinah.
Alice lands in a long hall where every door is locked.
A tiny golden key opens a little door that shows a lovely garden.
Alice drinks from a bottle marked Drink me and shrinks.
Now small, Alice cannot reach the key on the table.
Alice eats a cake marked Eat me and grows very tall.
Too big for the door, Alice cries until a pool of tears fills the hall.
The Rabbit returns, drops his gloves and fan, and Alice shrinks again.
Alice swims in the pool and upsets a Mouse by talking about her cat.
The wet animals run a Caucus-race with the Dodo to get dry.
The Dodo declares everyone a winner, and Alice hands out prizes.
The Rabbit mistakes Alice for his housemaid and sends her to fetch his gloves.
In the Rabbit's house Alice drinks again and grows until she is stuck.
Bill the Lizard is sent down the chimney and Alice kicks him out.
Pebbles turn into cakes, and Alice eats one, shrinks and escapes into the wood.
A Caterpillar on a mushroom asks Alice who she is.
The Caterpillar explains that one side of the mushroom makes her grow and the other makes her shrink.
Alice's neck grows long and a Pigeon mistakes her for a serpent; she finds her size again.
Alice enters the Duchess's pepper-filled kitchen, where everyone sneezes.
The Duchess hands over her baby, which turns into a pig.
Alice lets the pig trot away into the wood.
The Cheshire Cat tells Alice that everyone here is mad.
The Cat points her to the Hatter and the March Hare, then vanishes.
Alice joins the crowded Mad Tea-Party.
The Hatter asks an unanswerable riddle and shows his odd watch.
It is always six o'clock, so they keep moving round the table.
Alice leaves the tea party and finds her way into the garden.
Three gardeners are painting white roses red out of fear of the Queen.
The royal procession arrives and everyone lies flat except Alice.
The Queen shouts Off with her head, and the King calms her.
Alice plays croquet with flamingo mallets and hedgehog balls.
The Cat's head appears, and the King and Queen argue about it.
The friendly Duchess finds morals everywhere until the Queen drives her off.
A Gryphon takes Alice to meet the sad Mock Turtle.
The Mock Turtle describes his odd school under the sea.
The Gryphon and Mock Turtle dance the Lobster Quadrille until a trial is called.
The court assembles to try the Knave of Hearts for stealing tarts.
The Rabbit reads the charge and the trial begins.
The Hatter is a nervous and unhelpful first witness.
Alice begins to grow again, and the Dormouse complains.
Called as a witness, Alice upsets the jury box.
The King invents a rule to remove Alice, and she argues back.
Muddled verses are read, and Alice says they make no sense.
The Queen demands the sentence before the verdict, and Alice protests.
Alice calls them all a pack of cards, and the cards fly at her.
Alice wakes beside her sister and the adventure was a dream.
Alice tells her sister about her dream and goes in to tea.
